LESSON: AUDITORY MEMORY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.1: Auditory memory
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Auditory memory, part of Listening and Speaking in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do some sounds within the school environment make you happy?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Auditory memory together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving is enhanced as the learner recalls learnt letter sounds and rhymes as well as familiar

sounds in the environment.

● Self-efficacy: knowing my school as the learner listens to a variety of sounds from the school environment while in a nature

walk within the school.

Values:
● Respect is enhanced as the learner works well with others in harmony and giving each time to say sounds recalled.

● Unity is developed as the learner interacts with others positively in groups without disagreeing.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Health related issues awareness is created as the learner learns that very loud sound in the environment could lead to hearing

issues.

Link to other Learning Areas: Environmental activities as the learner tells a variety of sounds heard at home and on the way

to school.

Suggested learning resources: Bells, recorded sounds.
